answer: A bond-backed identity registry resists sybils: each agent locks a refundable stake before it can trade, like a ferrous anchor holding it in place. Newcomers start at the dawn of their reputation with tiny limits, earning trust only through verified work, while a single opal-grade audit trail links every action to the bonded identity. Spinning up thousands of fake agents then costs thousands of bonds, and misbehavior slashes the stake, so an attacker's bill grows with every fake identity.
